title: Два приглашения на вечер  (Two Invitations for the Evening)

segments.t: While Sasha calls Max on the phone to check if he has packed his suitcase for their flight to Cyprus, Vika calls him moments later and asks him to come over to her apartment that evening to talk. Meanwhile in the kitchen, a sheepish Chef Barinov admits to Lyova that Valdemar turned out to be a decent man after all.
Я уже почти готова и чемодан тоже.
Ты как?
В смысле, я нет.
В смысле, в процессе.
Целую. Да.
Макс, я думаю, нам все-таки нужно поговорить.
Ты можешь приехать сегодня ко мне?
Или ты занят?
Как раз сегодня я абсолютно свободен.
Буду ждать.
А все-таки Вальдемар хороший человек.
Да, если он хороший, значит, я плохой.
А я не плохой.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
Я уже почти готова и чемодан тоже.
'I am almost ready and my suitcase is packed too.' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'some' in spoken Russian.
Ты как?
'How about you?' In Russian, the idea of 'you' flows naturally into 'how' without extra filler words. Max answers right away.
В смысле, я нет.
'I mean, I am not.' Max anchors the line on 'sense', while 'there is no' completes the thought.
В смысле, в процессе.
'I mean, I am in the middle of it.' In Russian, the idea of 'sense' flows naturally into 'process' without extra filler words.
Целую. Да.
'Kisses. Yes.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'am kissing' before landing on 'yes'. Kostya answers right away.
Макс, я думаю, нам все-таки нужно поговорить.
'Max, I think we really do need to talk.' The grammar packs 'Max' and 'to talk' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Ты можешь приехать сегодня ко мне?
'Can you come over to my place tonight?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'you' and finishing on 'for me'.
Или ты занят?
'Or are you busy?' Notice how Russian expresses 'or' and 'busy' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
Как раз сегодня я абсолютно свободен.
'As a matter of fact, tonight I am completely free.' The meaning hinges on 'how' working together with 'free' in spoken Russian.
Буду ждать.
'I will be waiting.' Notice how Russian expresses 'will' and 'to wait for' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
А все-таки Вальдемар хороший человек.
'Still, Valdemar is a good man.' Max anchors the line on 'and', while 'man' completes the thought. Kostya answers right away.
Да, если он хороший, значит, я плохой.
'Yes, and if he is good, that means I am bad.' In Russian, the idea of 'yes' flows naturally into 'bad' without extra filler words.
А я не плохой.
'And I am not bad.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'bad'. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
